results.note: Drops the sorted() normalization so item tuples are hashed in whatever order market.items iterates, making the fingerprint order-dependent instead of order-stable.
Swaps the explicit None-check for truthiness; a market object with a falsy __bool__/__len__ would be wrongly treated as absent.
Drops sell_price from the per-item tuple, so a sell-price-only change no longer alters the fingerprint.
Drops result.reason from the hashed tuple (member replaced by a constant), so a reason-only change no longer changes the fingerprint.
Changes the missing-market_id default from None to empty string, silently altering the hash input whenever location/market_id is absent.

Drops result.station from the hashed tuple -- the exact regression: two stations with no market hash identical. (Replaces the generator's encode-errors mutant, whose anchor occurs three times in the file.)
Drops result.system from the hashed tuple. (Replaces the generator's md5 mutant, whose anchor occurs three times in the file.)
Swaps the module-level market_fingerprint(result) call for the closure's local _fingerprint(grid), fingerprinting the wrong object entirely.
Requires a trailing CRLF instead of LF to consider a line complete; plain LF-terminated lines are wrongly treated as partial and never consumed.
Off-by-one boundary mutation: under-advances the consumed offset by one byte per line, causing byte drift and eventual re-reads or corruption.
Removes the guard that stops at a partial final line; the loop falls through and consumes the incomplete tail instead of leaving it for the next poll.
Off-by-one boundary mutation on the final offset commit, causing the last consumed byte to be re-read (and possibly re-parsed) on the next poll.
Drops the strip() normalization, so a blank line (which still carries its trailing newline byte) is no longer recognized as empty and is passed on to json.loads.
